about: The plugins and their pictures, for the website and the READMEs. npm run showcase makes the pictures in a demo home; test/site-manifest.test.js checks this file against the plugin folders and their package.json.

plugins.name: coordinator
plugins.title: Coordinator
plugins.tagline: Any chat can run its work in threads that report back to it.
plugins.summary: Type /coordinate in a chat, and the chat can start threads. Each thread is a DSH session that does one task in the chat's folder and hands its result back to the chat. The chat keeps its model, its permission and your tools, and you can open any thread and talk to it.
features: Turn it on with /coordinate or the Coordinate button; /coordinate off stops it.
Threads are ordinary DSH sessions, listed live under the chat that started them.
A thread hands back when it is done, blocked or needs a decision. The handback is the chat's next turn.
New threads start on the model and effort in the chat's Thread settings.
A thread that stops without a handback gets one nudge, then the chat gets a short note.

plugins.name: decisions
plugins.title: Decisions
plugins.tagline: One inbox for everything waiting on you. Answer in place.
plugins.summary: When a session needs you, Decisions shows it as a card: what is asked, what the agent recommends, which session and how long it has waited. Your answer goes into the session. The session's own log proves that it arrived, and the card says so.
features: Cards for decision lines, tools waiting for approval, questions in DSH's question box and threads that need a decision.
Each card shows the question, the recommendation, the session (one click opens it) and the wait.
An answer steers a running turn, starts the next turn of an idle session, or settles the approval or question.
Each delivery is proven by the session's log, and the card says so, or says why not.
Optional: a short note for each new card to a webhook or a command.
requires: Optional: Notifications, to hear of new cards outside the window

plugins.name: recall
plugins.title: Recall
plugins.tagline: Search everything you already did, and open each result at its exact turn.
plugins.summary: Recall keeps a full-text index of your past work on this computer: this DSH's sessions and, when you name them, other DSH homes, coding-agent transcript folders and Markdown handoff notes. Type a few words, and it lists the best turns with the words marked. A result opens its session at that turn.
features: A local index that grows as you work. Nothing leaves this computer.
Filters by folder, model, date and kind.
A result opens its session at that exact turn, scrolled to it and marked.
Agents search the same index with the recall_search tool.
requires: Node 22.15 or newer, DSH's own runtime (for SQLite and zstd)

screenshots.caption: Search past work: the best turns first, with the words marked, and filters for kind, time, folder and model.

screenshots.caption: Agents search the same index with the recall_search tool.

plugins.name: proof
plugins.title: Proof
plugins.tagline: Checks each claim of done, passed, fixed or deployed against what its turn ran.
plugins.summary: When a reply says that something is done, passing, fixed or deployed, Proof reads what that turn ran: tool output, exit codes, test counts, metric changes and file hashes. A claim that nothing shows, or that the turn's own output contradicts, gets a short card after the turn. Proof keeps every claim in a ledger that you can export.
features: Shown: something in the turn shows the claim, and Proof stays quiet.
No evidence: nothing in the turn shows it, and a card says so.
Contradicted: the turn's own output says otherwise, and the card quotes it.
A ledger of every claim, which you can export.
Optional: an independent read-only check on a local model.

screenshots.caption: The ledger: every claim of a session, flagged or shown, with export to Markdown, CSV or JSON.

plugins.name: autopilot
plugins.title: Autopilot
plugins.tagline: Keeps sessions moving when nobody is watching.
plugins.summary: When a restart, a crash or a reload cuts off a running turn, Autopilot tells the session to carry on. When a session goes quiet with open todos, it gives one nudge, and it backs off when nudges bring no progress. When a turn fails, it tells the session to carry on after a wait, and it starts a stopped goal again. Every action says what it did and why.
features: A carry-on note after a restart, a crash or a reload cuts off a turn.
One nudge for a quiet session with open todos, and a back-off when nudges bring no progress.
Starts an active goal again after a restart or an error stopped it.
Leaves a session alone while it waits on you.
Every action has a Why line, is proven by the session's own log, and has a kill switch.
requires: Optional: Notifications, to hear when it backs off or asks you something

screenshots.caption: Its page: what waits for you, what it backed off from, and a rule for each session: Auto, Ask first or Off.

plugins.name: agent-terminals
plugins.title: Agent Terminals
plugins.tagline: Command-line coding agents in DSH, each in a terminal tab beside its own session.
plugins.summary: Name a program and the folder it works in. Agent Terminals gives it a DSH session of its own, starts it in a terminal of that session, and shows the terminal in a tab beside the session. Your messages go in one at a time, and the agent's own transcript proves that it read them.
features: The agent's state (working, idle, waiting on you, stopped) on the Coding agents page, on its session's row and in Decisions.
Your messages go in one at a time, and are delivered only when the transcript shows them.
It presses no key while a tool call or an approval prompt is open in the agent.
After DSH restarts, each agent starts again under the same name and resumes its conversation.
requires: A command-line coding agent that you run in a terminal

plugins.name: canon
plugins.title: Canon
plugins.tagline: Shared long-term memory from an Obsidian vault, added to each turn as a short cited block.
plugins.summary: Canon reads a vault of canon notes. When a turn starts, it finds the few active notes that fit the prompt and the session's folder, and adds them after the prompt as one short block that names the path of each note. When you allow drafts, agents can save draft notes, and only a person promotes a draft.
features: Recall: at most 3 notes and 2,000 characters by default, and you can turn it off for one session.
Capture: agents save drafts only when you allow it. Drafts are never added to a turn.
Promote or Discard a draft on Canon's page. Nothing promotes a draft by itself.
It reads the vault on this computer: no model call, no network.
requires: An Obsidian vault: a folder of Markdown notes

plugins.name: calendar
plugins.title: Calendar
plugins.tagline: Your calendars in DSH, for you and your agents.
plugins.summary: Calendar syncs iCloud, Google, Microsoft 365, Fastmail, Nextcloud and other CalDAV calendars, subscribed .ics feeds, and calendars kept in DSH. It sends each change to the server that holds the event, so your phone and your other apps see it too. Agents read your calendars and change them as their permission allows.
features: iCloud, Google, Microsoft 365, Outlook.com, Fastmail, Nextcloud, Yahoo and any other CalDAV server.
Subscribed .ics feeds, read only, and calendars kept in DSH itself.
Passwords and sign-ins stay in DSH's credential store, never in the plugin's files or its log.
Agents change events as the chat's permission allows. DSH's approval prompt asks you first on Workspace Write.
A change that emails someone always asks you first, and says who gets what.
requires: An account with a calendar service, or none for calendars kept in DSH
For Google or Microsoft: an OAuth client or app registration of your own

plugins.name: discord
plugins.title: Discord
plugins.tagline: A Discord bot for your own channels: each conversation gets a thread and its own DSH session.
plugins.summary: A message in one of the bot's channels gets a thread made from it, and that thread gets its own DSH session. Every later message in the thread goes to the same session, also after DSH restarts. The agent answers in the thread with the discord_send tool.
features: One thread, one DSH session, kept across restarts.
Every turn ends with an answer in the thread: a turn that forgets is reminded once.
It answers only in the channels and to the people that you allow.
Slash commands in the thread: /status, /stop, /new, /reset, /rename, /model and /effort.
requires: A Discord application with a bot token of your own

plugins.name: session-watch
plugins.title: Session Watch
plugins.tagline: The shared watcher behind Autopilot, Decisions and Agent Terminals.
plugins.summary: Session Watch reads the state of every session once, from DSH's own events, and serves it to the other suite plugins, so they never read session logs or poll. It has no page of its own. Its part in Plugins shows what it watches: how many sessions there are, how many run, and how many wait on you.
features: Each session's state: running, waiting for approval, waiting for your answer, cut off, idle and more.
Choose a state in Plugins to list its sessions.
Delivery of a message, proven by the session's own log, for the plugins that send one.
One reader of DSH's events for the whole suite.

plugins.name: categories
plugins.title: Categories
plugins.tagline: Group your workspaces into categories in DSH's session list.
plugins.summary: Categories puts a header for each category over its workspaces in DSH's session list, then Other workspaces for the rest. You make and arrange categories from the list or from the Categories page. With the coordinator plugin on too, a coordinating chat and its threads stay in their workspace, and the workspace stays in its category.
features: A header for each category over its workspaces, and Other workspaces for the rest.
Make, rename, move and delete categories from the session list or the Categories page.
Works with DSH's own rows, and with the coordinator's threads.
It needs no settings.

plugins.name: reasoning-pill
plugins.title: Reasoning pill
plugins.tagline: One place to set reasoning: a Reasoning control beside the model name.
plugins.summary: A Reasoning control sits beside the model name in the composer and changes the session's reasoning effort. While it runs, DSH's own Effort row in the model menu is hidden, so there is one reasoning control. The plugin keeps no data, has no settings and adds no routes.
features: The model's levels, in DSH's words, in a menu above the control.
The session's log records each pick, and the next request to the model carries it.
New chats start at your last pick.
Switched off, DSH's Effort row comes back at once.

plugins.name: notifications
plugins.title: Notifications
plugins.tagline: System notifications while you are not using DSH's window.
plugins.summary: Other plugins send their news through it: the coordinator when a thread hands back, Decisions for each new card, Agent Terminals when an agent waits on you, Autopilot when it backs off. It shows news while you are not using DSH, and a click brings DSH's window up on the chat that the news is about.
features: Shows with DSH's icon, from DSH's own window, while its window is hidden, behind others or idle.
A click brings DSH's window up on the chat that the news is about.
Built for long runs: you leave DSH working, and the news finds you.
Its page lists the recent notifications and what happened to each.
requires: A DSH window that can show notifications: the Desktop app, or DSH's web profile in a browser tab
platforms: Linux and Windows (their senders have unit tests only)

plugins.name: wallpaper
plugins.title: Wallpaper
plugins.tagline: Your wallpapers behind DSH, with frosted glass, colour mode and motion.
plugins.summary: A picture or a colour sits behind DSH, and DSH's sidebar, open chat, right dock and composer become frosted glass over it. An optional headline replaces DSH's words on the new-chat page. You set everything in one panel, from a button in the sidebar footer.
features: A wallpaper library with collections, rotation and colours.
Frosted glass on the sidebar, the open chat, the right dock and the composer.
Colour mode: Dark, Light or System.
An optional headline on the new-chat page.
Visual only: it changes DSH's grounds, never DSH's text, icons or controls.

plugins.name: dsh-site
plugins.title: DSH Site
plugins.tagline: Opens this Mac's DSH window to the devices on your private network.
plugins.summary: Your phone, tablet or laptop on your tailnet opens this Mac's address on port 8443 and gets the same DSH: the same sessions, workspaces and tools. Nothing is copied or synced. DSH Site lets in only the devices that you list, checks every request the way DSH does, and passes it on to DSH's own server.
features: The same DSH on every device of your tailnet: no copy, no sync.
An address gate: only the devices and networks that you list get in.
DSH's own cross-site and DNS-rebinding checks on every request.
A device signs in once with DSH's sign-in link and stays signed in for up to 30 days.
requires: A private network, such as a Tailscale tailnet

plugins.name: session-bridge
plugins.title: Session Bridge
plugins.tagline: Lets scripts and scheduled jobs on this Mac start, prompt, steer and read DSH sessions.
plugins.summary: Session Bridge is a small JSON API for the running DSH, on a Unix socket that only your user can open. Scripts, cron jobs and other agents create, prompt, steer, cancel and read sessions, and wait for a reply without polling. A session made through the bridge shows live in the DSH window, where you can take over.
features: A Unix socket only, mode 600: no TCP port.
Safe retries with your own request id: one session for each create, and no prompt sent twice.
Wait for the end of a turn in one call, with its reply.
Steer a running turn, or queue a follow-up.
The log records actions and sizes, never a prompt's text.
